sources.title: Paleobiological remarks on a new partial skeleton of the Eocene Antarctic penguin Palaeeudyptes klekowskii
sources.author: Carolina Acosta Hospitaleche2016, Ameghiniana53(3):269–281
sources.evidence: Original13-page paper read; Fig1 author schematic not to scale and Fig3 shoulder/Fig4 femur actual photos inspected. MLP12-I-20-289 femur131.5mm/coracoid165mm, allometric body length133.2–143.2cm and mass40–44kg. No skull/complete wing preserved in this specimen.

sources.title: Bill disparity and feeding strategies among fossil and modern penguins
sources.author: 2020, Paleobiology46(2):176–192
sources.evidence: Long spear-like Eocene bill fossils initially only tentatively assigned Palaeeudyptes or Anthropornis. Not genus-specific associated cranial evidence.

sources.title: First articulated skeleton of Palaeeudyptes gunnari from late Eocene Seymour Island
sources.author: Acosta Hospitaleche and Reguero2010
sources.evidence: MLP96-I-6-13 is a specifically assigned articulated postcranial skeleton; confirms genus comparison but not same individual or species as2016anchor.
